title: Glossary.
caption: Four terms mean different things in the two projects: interpreter, `execute`, recovery and expiry.
rows: A bounded set of rules the owner installs so an app can act without a prompt for each call
No single object: one context rule per contract, each with its policies
The JSON a wallet submits to install a grant; an input and a hash commitment
The rules and metadata stored under a grant ID, stamped with the grant generation
The owner's account policy: administrative rules and recovery configuration
Rule 0 and the account's other context rules
One target contract, function list, argument conditions and signer threshold, with optional expiry, cap and generation
The contract whose functions a rule lets be called
Which listed signers must approve: a threshold over distinct identities
The rule's signers, with a threshold policy attached
Key material plus a verifier contract that checks evidence for it (Ed25519, WebAuthn passkey)
Same kind; refused on rules the interpreter polices (error {{fact:opb-error-external-signer}})
Another Soroban address that approves through the host (CAP-0071)
Same kind; the only kind on policed rules
A contract with `verify(digest, key, signature) -> bool`
The same interface for External signers
A stateless contract that parses and validates a document, resolves verifier names and returns canonical bytes, `doc_hash` and a model
The account code around the evaluator: installs documents, authenticates signers, stores state, admits recovery completion; tested, not proved
The pure function that decides an authorization and returns the next spending records
A capped rule's charged amounts and their ledgers
At most *limit* charged over the last *P* ledgers: the window at ledger *L* is (*L* − *P*, *L*]
A counter on the account, 0 at creation, advanced only by a completed recovery; a grant from an older generation refuses
A counter that every recovery-configuration change, completed recovery and executed upgrade advances
A counter that every account-document write and executed upgrade advances
The recovery controller's counter; it invalidates older evidence and attempts
The adopted recovery controller and the zero-knowledge adapter and pool; no grant rule may call them
Removing a stale grant's rules, tags and spending records; anyone may do it
An entry whose rent lapsed: unavailable until restored, never absent
One call (contract, function, arguments) in the invocation tree the host passes to `__check_auth`
The same; a context rule matches it
Signed credentials for one invocation tree; the host consumes its nonce when the transaction succeeds
OpenZeppelin's unit of authorization: a context type, signers, policies and an optional `valid_until`
A contract attached to a context rule; the account calls its `enforce` after authenticating (hooks `install`, `uninstall`, `enforce`)
The expression the interpreter stores per (account, rule) and evaluates in `enforce`
An oz-policy-builder contract whose `execute(calls, grants, wait)` runs a batch for the account, bound to one custody gate or none
A rule with no signer, bound to an execution adapter; anyone may run what its predicate permits
Perch {{fact:perch-deployed-account-version}}'s policy contract; its address is still pinned and reported, never called
The account's owner-authorized call as the account
The adapter's batch call `execute(calls, grants, wait)`
Replacing lost credentials through guardians, a zero-knowledge proof, or both
The Prime app's "recovery" moves custody funds to a fixed address
Recovery profiles: Loss assumes a key may be lost but not stolen; Protected assumes it may be stolen
An address whose approval counts toward the recovery condition
A value spent at completion so one zero-knowledge proof cannot complete two recoveries
Perch's canonical JSON (RFC 8785 restricted to Perch documents) and the SHA-256 of a document's canonical bytes
The interpreter's `predicate_hash` over a predicate's bytes
The Rust compiler's mid-level intermediate representation, from which the proofs start
Tools that read MIR and translate Rust into a pure Lean program
The proof assistant whose kernel checks the theorems
An HTTP payment protocol; proposed as a payment integration for an agent runtime
